string.text: When Instant identify is on, keep the normal scanning wait while hip-firing (only ADS / binoculars stay instant). No effect unless Instant identify is on.
When Instant identify is on, keep the normal scanning wait while aiming down sight. No effect unless Instant identify is on.
When Instant identify is on, keep the normal scanning wait while looking through binoculars. No effect unless Instant identify is on.
Click, then press a key to bind it.
Optional modifier held with the identify key.

Which visual language the tag uses: Card (full details), Minimal (faction-coloured dot with a relation sign), Bodycam (faction-coloured outline box locked to the head), Simple 2 (faction circle plus relation triangle over the head), Simple (dot, faction logo and name strip), Crooks (one static screen readout of the last target), Minimal 2 (a bare relation-coloured dot), or Patch (the faction patch ringed by a relation-coloured outline).
Bodycam style: draw the outline rectangle around just the head/face, or around the full body.
Bodycam style: colour the outline rectangle by faction, or by relationship (red enemy / green friendly / grey neutral).
Bodycam style: thickness of the outline rectangle's edges, in pixels.
Bodycam style: extra margin around the model so the outline isn't tight against it. A fraction of the box size (0 = tight, 0.20 = 20% larger each side), so it stays proportional at any distance.
Bodycam style: opacity of the outline rectangle (1 = solid, lower = more transparent). The name/faction/weapon text is unaffected.

Bodycam style: space in pixels between the outline box and the name / faction / weapon text beside it. Raise it if a thick outline or a large box padding crowds the text. 0 puts the text flush against the box.
Patch style: size of the faction patch in pixels, at the reference distance. The patch and its outline scale with distance from there (near = bigger, far = smaller).
Patch style: thickness of the relationship outline around the patch, in pixels at the reference distance. 0 = no outline at all, just the bare faction patch.
Patch style: gap between the faction patch and its relationship outline, in pixels at the reference distance. 0 = the outline sits flush against the patch.

Continuously identify every target in your view and within range, without pressing the key or aiming at them. Line of sight is always required. Pairs well with the Bodycam style. (If Only show overlay while aimed is on, only aimed targets are kept.)

Auto-identify while hip-firing (not aiming down sight, not through binoculars) once a target has been held on your aim (or inside the FOV assist range, if that's on) for the hold time below. For players who'd rather not press the key and still identify from the hip. You can track a moving target; aiming at empty air does nothing.
How long a target must stay under your hip-fire aim (or in the FOV assist range) before it auto-identifies. Set to 0 to identify instantly the moment you aim at a target, with no wait. Default 1.0 s.
Hard cutoff on the effective identify range while hip-firing (not aiming down sight, not through binoculars). Caps the base identification distance after any scaling. 0 = no cap.
Tint the tag by your relation to the target: red enemy, green friend, tan neutral. Off = a flat neutral tint. This is about COLOUR only - to drop the relationship cue entirely, use Show relation.
Show the target's name line. Applies to every style that draws text (Card and Bodycam).
Show the target's faction line on styles that draw text (Card and Bodycam). In Minimal style it toggles the faction-coloured dot.
Show the target's rank line (Card and Bodycam, and below the name in the Crooks readout).

Show whether the target is hostile, friendly or neutral. Off = the tag tells you who they are but never how they feel about you: no relation sign in Minimal, no triangle in Simple 2, no relation tint on the Card or Simple, no outline at all in Patch (the outline IS the relation cue there), and Bodycam / Minimal 2 fall back to the faction colour.

Use your own faction patch art instead of the game's built-in faction icons. The tag then asks for the texture id "ii_patch_" plus the faction id - ii_patch_duty, ii_patch_freedom, ii_patch_stalker and so on - which you register yourself in a textures_descr XML alongside your .dds files. Nothing ships for these ids, and a faction you have not provided a patch for simply shows no patch, so add art for every faction you expect to meet. Takes effect immediately, including on tags already on screen. Off by default.
Show the target's currently-wielded weapon and its caliber. Applies to every style that draws text (Card and Bodycam).
Skip the scan wait and spinner entirely -- the tag reveals immediately on identify. Overrides Scan delay and all scan-time modifiers.
How long the scan pulses before the tag reveals.
Fade in/out duration of the tag.
How long the tag stays fully visible after identification (while the target remains in sight; out-of-sight targets drop sooner, see "Drop tag when out of sight").

The BASE range identification works at, before it's scaled up (binocular/ADS magnification, range boosts) or down (distance/other penalties). It is not a hard maximum -- the effective range can end up higher or lower. To hard-cap the effective range, use the "Max identification distance" cutoffs on the Hipfire / ADS / Binoculars pages.
When you don't land a direct hit, identify the nearest target within the on-screen assist circle. Turn off to require aiming directly at the target.

For free-aim setups (e.g. bodycam): center the assist on where you're actually aiming instead of the screen center. Firearms work on any engine (via the weapon trace); a knife or raised binoculars need the custom bodycam engine's aim binding. Harmless otherwise — it just falls back to the screen center.
Aim tolerance for picking a target without a direct hit. Measured as an angle from where you aim, so it works the same whether hip-firing or scoped at any magnification (0 = direct hit only).

Shrink the target-assist radius by however much your optic magnifies, so the assist forgives the same amount of real-world aim error scoped as unscoped. Without this, a fixed pixel radius covers a much wider area of the world the further you zoom in, making the assist grabbier exactly where you are aiming most carefully. Off = the radius is a flat screen distance at every zoom level.

For the hipfire / ADS / binocular auto-triggers: reveal EVERY eligible target inside the target-assist radius, so a cluster of stacked stalkers all get identified at once. Turn off to identify only the single target nearest your aim point. (A manual keypress always identifies the nearest one. Auto-identify visible targets is not affected.) On by default.
Only pick targets you can actually see.

Treat see-through surfaces -- chain-link fences, glass, foliage, and invisible clip meshes -- as solid for line of sight, so you cannot identify a target through them. Off (default): identification sees through them (only opaque walls block). Applies wherever line of sight is checked (always for auto-identify; for manual identify when Require line of sight is on).

Block identification through foliage specifically (bushes, trees, grass) while still seeing through fences and glass. A lighter version of "Block ID through transparent surfaces." Best-effort by material name -- if some plants aren't caught, use the full transparent-surfaces block instead.

Don't allow an entity that is actively hostile toward you and aware of you -- one that has pulled aggro and will attack -- to be an identification target. Detected from its AI combat target and its enemy relation + line of sight to you. The target-assist skips such enemies and picks another target; a target you identified BEFORE combat has its tag removed the moment it turns hostile and engages you. Off by default.

Only ever track the target you're aiming at or near (within the FOV radius of your aim point). Aiming away DROPS it -- so aiming back re-runs the whole scan from scratch rather than instantly reappearing. Scopes identification to the aimed target (auto-identify won't fill the screen). Default off.
Drop tag when out of sight

Remove an active tag as soon as its target goes out of sight (behind cover or off-screen), instead of waiting out the visibility duration. A brief occlusion is tolerated; re-identify (or auto-identify) brings it back.
Also auto-identify on a steady aim through raised binoculars, alongside the normal key.
Identification only works while actively looking through raised binoculars.
How long to hold aim steady before auto-identifying.
Whether FOV target assist also applies while looking through raised binoculars. Turn off to require a direct hit when using binoculars.
Faster reveal and longer range with binoculars raised, any mode.
Scan speed multiplier while binoculars are raised.
Max (and fade-out) distance multiplier while binoculars are raised. A flat multiplier by default, or the x1 base when "Scale range by magnification" (below) is on.

Multiply the binocular range by the binocular's magnification (like the ADS option), so the range tracks the optical zoom instead of a flat multiplier. Off = flat "Binoculars max distance multiplier". On: set that multiplier to 1.0 for range = base x magnification.

Wipe every identified target the moment you stop looking through the binoculars, including ones still close enough to identify normally. Targets beyond your normal range already disappear on their own when you lower them (the magnified range goes away with the magnification); this option clears the rest too, making glassing strictly live observation - what you saw through the optic is gone as soon as it leaves your eyes.

Hard cutoff on the effective identify range through binoculars. Caps the base identification distance after magnification/boost scaling -- use this to stop high-magnification binoculars from reaching absurdly far. 0 = no cap.

Auto-identify while aiming down sight once a target has been held on your aim (or inside the FOV assist range, if that's on) for the hold time below, alongside the normal key. You can track a moving target; aiming at empty air does nothing.

How long (seconds) a target must stay on your aim (or in FOV assist range) while aiming down sight before it auto-identifies, in ADS mode. Set to 0 to identify instantly the moment you aim at a target, with no wait.
Faster reveal and longer range while aiming down sight, any mode.
Scan speed multiplier while aiming down sight (lower = faster).
Max (and fade-out) distance multiplier while aiming down sight. This is the base for a 1x sight; higher-power scopes scale it up if zoom scaling is on.

Multiply the ADS range by the scope's magnification (x2, x4, ...), so higher-power optics reach further. Works with PiP scopes and, on engines without PiP, from the aim FOV. Iron sights stay near the x1 base.
While aiming down sight, suppress all main-view identification tags for a clean sight picture. In-scope markers (if any) still draw.
Hard cutoff on the effective identify range while aiming down sight. Caps the base identification distance after magnification/boost scaling. 0 = no cap.
Draw identification markers inside a Picture-in-Picture scope's lens. Needs a PiP-capable engine; when off, the mod behaves as if there were no PiP support (normal HUD, no in-scope markers).
Hide main-view UI when scope is up
While a PiP scope is rendering, suppress all main-view identification tags, leaving only the in-scope UI.
Flat size multiplier, not distance-based. Despite the name it scales EVERY style, not just the Card - for the styles that scale with distance it multiplies on top of that.

Card style: scale the faction emblem on the plate up or down. 1.25 is the default. The plate widens to match, so the text never crowds it, and the emblem is capped to the plate height when the card is short.
Simple style: scale the faction emblem in the strip up or down. 1.25 is the default. The strip re-centres itself around the new size, so the marker stays on the target.
Card style only: below this scale the card no longer fits, so just the relation dot is shown instead.
In the Minimal (dot) style, size the dot by distance so a far target's dot isn't oversized (near = bigger, far = smaller). Off = a flat size like the other styles.
Horizontal nudge for the on-screen UI elements (card / dot / box), in virtual pixels. Negative = left.
Vertical nudge for the on-screen UI elements (card / dot / box), in virtual pixels. Negative = up.

Where on the target the tag / marker is drawn: Head (default), Torso, or Feet. Applies to the card and all dot styles (and the in-scope marker); the Bodycam box keeps its own Head/Body setting. Monsters without a skeleton fall back to the head anchor.
Further targets take longer to scan.
Scan time multiplier at max range. Binoculars mitigate this for free by extending max range itself.
Higher-ranked stalkers take longer to identify than a rookie.
Scan time multiplier for the highest rank (legend), vs. a rookie.

Each target's actual scene luminance controls the slowdown: shadows and darkness increase it, while flashlights and other illumination reduce it. World time is used as a fallback when object luminance is unavailable.
When the actor's night-vision goggles are switched on, low target visibility does not increase scan time.
Scan time multiplier for a target at zero luminance.
Target luminance at which the visibility penalty ends. The engine reports 0 for complete darkness and 1 for bright light. Default 0.50.
Rain exposure, storms, and fog make targets harder to read. The strongest current obstruction sets one combined slowdown, so rain and its related effects are not counted repeatedly.
Scan time multiplier at maximum weather or wet-visor obstruction. Fog scales with the target's distance; rain and storms only apply while exposed.
Use Anomaly/GAMMA's accumulated gas-mask droplet level as another visibility obstruction. Soft integration: it has no effect when that droplet state is unavailable or no mask is active.
Normalized visor-droplet level where its slowdown begins (0 = immediately, 0.95 = only when almost fully covered). The penalty then ramps to the maximum visibility slowdown at full coverage.
Apply a scan-time penalty while enemies are actively fighting the actor. Combat remains active briefly after enemies lose their target to avoid flickering between states.
Total scan-time multiplier during general combat.
Total scan-time multiplier after a direct combat hit or hostile bullet passes nearby. This temporarily replaces the general combat multiplier.
How long the stronger under-fire slowdown remains after each hit or near miss.
How close a hostile bullet must pass to count as being shot at.
The heavier the item you're currently holding, the longer identification takes -- a heavy weapon is harder to hold steady enough to read a target. Uses the item's inventory weight. Off by default.
Scan time multiplier when holding an item at (or above) the reference weight, vs. a weightless item.
Held-item weight (kg) at which the penalty reaches its maximum; lighter items scale down linearly toward no penalty at 0. E.g. 6 kg maxes the slowdown for a heavy weapon while a pistol stays light.

Identifying a target through foliage (bushes, trees, grass on the line of sight) takes longer -- the plants partly obscure them. A soft alternative to "Block ID through foliage": you can still read a target through a bush, it just takes more time. Off by default.
Scan time multiplier when the sightline to the target crosses a foliage material. Applied as a flat multiplier (e.g. 2.5 = two-and-a-half times as long).
Re-identifying someone you've identified before is faster.
Scan time multiplier for a previously-identified target.
Identifying gets faster with a higher Skill System perception level (needs the optional FOMOD component).
Scan time reduction per perception level.
Perception experience granted on a successful identify.
Bonus perception experience granted the first time you loot a corpse you'd already identified.
Write aim/trace diagnostics to the game log (xray_*.log) on each identify attempt. For troubleshooting free-aim target acquisition. Leave off normally.

On-screen visualiser for the FOV target-assist: a RED dot at the current aim point, a YELLOW ring showing the assist radius (fov_radius, with its value as text), and dots on the bones of every entity whose body falls inside the ring -- GREEN if within identify range, RED if the target is beyond max range -- each labelled with its distance in metres. Also shows the current scope magnification and the effective max range (base widened by the binocular/ADS boost). For tuning fov_radius / max range / diagnosing target acquisition. Leave off normally.

TESTING: makes the mod behave as if the custom engine bindings (bodycam free-aim / in-scope markers and the SVP/PiP magnification) were not compiled in, so it runs its stock-engine fallbacks. Lets you test on a stock exe without copying the custom one. Does not affect stock bindings (weapon trace, raycast). Leave off for normal play.
Which screen corner the Crooks readout (FACTION | NAME of the last identified stalker) anchors to. Fine-tune with the X/Y offsets below.
Horizontal nudge of the Crooks readout from its corner anchor (+ = right).
Vertical nudge of the Crooks readout from its bottom anchor (+ = up).

Crooks style: scale the faction emblem up or down. 1.25 is the default; the emblem stays centred on the readout as it grows, so large values may need the Y offset raised to keep it clear of the screen edge. Does not affect the text.

Crooks style: space in pixels between the faction emblem and the text beside it. Independent of the patch size, so the spacing stays where you set it as the emblem grows or shrinks. 0 puts the text flush against the emblem.

Master toggle: when ON, the whole Wearable Devices integration is bypassed and identification works exactly as if this compatibility component were never installed (no scanner kit, no tiers, normal on-entity identification). All the other settings on this page have no effect while this is on.

When the wearable-devices compatibility is installed: block ALL identification unless the full kit is worn/assembled (scanner worn + Promin antenna module + a process module). Off = identification still works normally when the kit isn't complete, and the tiers only enhance it while the kit is worn. Only affects you if st-wearable-devices and the compatibility component are installed.

When the scanner finishes identifying a target that is hostile toward you, play that faction's warning sound. Plays once per identification, as the result appears. Works regardless of the Show relation setting, since it is a warning rather than a display. Factions without a warning sound (Ecologists, Zombified, traders, mutants, Arena) stay silent.
- Process module: scan time per tier (s) -
Base scan time with a Tier 1 process module. Default 1.5s.
Base scan time with a Tier 2 process module. Default 1.0s.
Base scan time with a Tier 3 process module. Default 0.5s.
- Process module: penalty strength per tier -
Share of every enabled scan penalty applied with a Tier 1 process module. 0 removes penalties, 1 applies their full configured slowdown, and 2 doubles the slowdown they add. Default 1.00.
Share of every enabled scan penalty applied with a Tier 2 process module. 0 removes penalties, 1 applies their full configured slowdown, and 2 doubles the slowdown they add. Default 0.75.
Share of every enabled scan penalty applied with a Tier 3 process module. 0 removes penalties, 1 applies their full configured slowdown, and 2 doubles the slowdown they add. Default 0.50.
Identify range with a Tier 1 scanner. Default 10m.
Identify range with a Tier 2 scanner. Default 20m.
Identify range with a Tier 3 scanner. Default 30m.
- Process tier that unlocks each data feature -
Which process-module tier reveals the target's faction. Default Tier 1.
Which process-module tier shows the distance to the target. Default Tier 1.
Which process-module tier reveals relationship (friend / enemy / neutral). Default Tier 2.
Which process-module tier reveals the target's rank. Default Tier 2.
Which process-module tier reveals the target's weapon and caliber. Default Tier 3.
- Scanner tier that unlocks each feature -
Which scanner tier enables identifying through raised binoculars (extends the identify range by the binocular range multiplier). Applies to both the AR and OSD channels. Default Tier 1.
Which scanner tier enables identifying while aiming down sights / through a scope. Default Tier 2.
Which scanner tier enables the scope-magnification range boost (reach further at higher zoom). Default Tier 2.
Which scanner tier removes the target-visibility scan-time penalty entirely. Default Tier 3.
Override the built-in faction, rank, and relation colors with your own R/G/B values below. Off = use the mod's default colors (the sliders are ignored). Applies live, no restart.
